caption:
In the 1950s, Quaker settlers arrived in the misty heights of Monteverde and turned to dairy farming to survive the rugged terrain. Today, those same high-altitude pastures, perched along the continental divide, produce some of Costa Rica's most celebrated cheeses. For travelers journeying slowly through the cloud forest, a simple meal of local cheese and fresh bread at a mountain kitchen door is the ultimate recovery fuel. It is honest, unhurried, and shaped entirely by the cool, damp climate of the highlands.
